summary: Takudo Ishikawa is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a research fellow at the Jodo Shu Research Institute (attested 2005-2006) and as a specially appointed full-time lecturer at Taisho University (attested 2015).

Takushu Sugimoto is an indologist, Buddhist studies scholar, and historian who earned his PhD from Tohoku University under teachers including Ensho Kanakura. He taught at Kanazawa University (~1978-2001), Komazawa University (attested 1990), and Kinjo University (~2001).
Tamara Cohen is an Indology and religious studies scholar who earned her PhD from the University of Toronto in 2023 under the supervision of Srilata Raman and Jürgen Hanneder.

Tampalawela Dhammaratana is a Buddhist studies scholar. He earned degrees from the University of Kelaniya, University of Paris under Jean-François Lyotard, Paris-Sorbonne University under Michel Hulin, and completed postdoctoral studies at École Pratique des Hautes Études under Pierre-Sylvain Filliozat.

Tan Chung is a historian and sinologist who earned a PhD from Visva-Bharati University. He served as Professor of Chinese at the University of Delhi (~1964-1978) and Head of Chinese and Japanese Studies at Jawaharlal Nehru University (~1978-1994).
Tan Poh Beng is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts at the International Buddhist College (attested 2015), supervised by Charles Willemen and Tilak Kariyawasam.
Tan Sitong (1865-1898) was a scholar in philosophy and Buddhist studies who studied under Yang Renshan (~1896-1898) and Wang Zhengyi.

Tan Yun-shan (1898-1983) was a scholar in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at Hunan Normal University and under teachers including Taixu, taught at Lida Academy (~1923-1927), and served as Professor of Chinese Studies at Visva-Bharati University (~1937-1968).
Tandin Dorji is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Tibetology who has worked as a lecturer at Sherubtse College and the National Institute of Education, Paro.

Tanero Sasakawa (1870-1949) was a scholar of Sinology, history, archaeology, and Japanology. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1893-1896) and held academic posts at Meiji University (~1904-1930) and Toyo University.

Tansen Sen is a historian, Buddhist studies scholar, and sinologist. Educated at Peking University and the University of Pennsylvania under Victor H. Mair, he held a post at Baruch College (attested 2003).
Tanso Hirose (1782-1856) was a scholar of Sinology and philosophy. He studied at Kamei Juku (~1797-1801) and under Hodō, and founded Kangien in 1801.

Tanzan Hara (1819-1892) was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied at Shoheizaka Gakumonjo. He was appointed Professor of Buddhist Studies at the University of Tokyo in 1879 and superintendent at Komazawa University in 1891.

Tao Jiang is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who earned his PhD from Temple University under Shigenori Nagatomo. He served as an Associate Professor of Religion at Rutgers University (attested 2011).
Tao Jin is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who completed a PhD at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign in 2008 under Alexander L. Mayer.
Tao Pan is a scholar in Indology and linguistics who earned a BA from Fudan University in 2010 and a Magister Artium from the University of Munich.
Tarab Tulku (1934-2004) was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He held posts as a curator at the Royal Danish Library (~1967-1998) and at the University of Copenhagen (~1968-1998).

Taranatha Tarkavachaspati (1812-1885) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He served as Professor of Grammar and Philosophy at Sanskrit College and University (~1845-1873) and as Professor of Sanskrit at Benares Sanskrit College.

Tarthang Tulku is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He taught at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (~1962-1968) and served as Head Lama of Padma Ling, the Tibetan Nyingma Meditation Center, and the Nyingma Institute.

Taryo Makita (1912-2011) was a Buddhist studies and Sinology scholar educated at Otani and Kyoto universities. He served as professor at Kyoto University (~1967-1976), Gifu University of Education (~1976-1986), and president of Saitama Institute of Technology (~1986-1994).
